20240101.text: ...Did that all get a little heavy for you? I think you prefer me when I'm just teasing you, don't you? Hehe...

20210302.text: That puppet was built with technology that has been lost to time. Perhaps she, as a god, is the only one privy to the knowledge of its origins...

20210303.text: Still... there is one other thing on this topic that I suspect you may be curious to know.

20210304.text: Before Ei began modifying her own godly form, she took it upon herself to create a prototype puppet...

20210305.text: So... you mean there are three Raiden Shoguns!?

20210306.text: No, the prototype was merely a proof of concept. Its appearance and intellect were not based on Ei. It was a test.

20210307.text: The original plan was for Ei to simply discard it. But perhaps Ei thought this to be too cruel, because in the end she chose only to seal the power within it.

20210308.text: Later, this puppet wandered Inazuma as an ordinary human male with his own consciousness, until... the Fatui took an interest in him.

20210310.text: Some eccentric geniuses in the ranks of the Fatui made adjustments to the prototype, not only unsealing his power, but very likely rendering him even more formidable than his original specifications.

20210312.text: Mm-hmm. The object of divine creation is the one who has now taken possession of the Gnosis... and the prototype puppet is now known as "The Balladeer."

20210313.text: What in the... What a crazy story!

20210314.text: It is, isn't it? Who can say whether it's coincidence or destiny.

745040201.text: Have you heard? Armand's been doing much better recently. He still gets nervous when there are too many people, but he can at least express what he means.

745040202.text: Well, he'd better be! How will he become a comedian if he stutters in front of people?

745040204.text: The staff member at Lepaute Horlogerie. You haven't seen him?

745040205.text: He's from the same village as us, and he wants to act in comedies. Unfortunately, he has a terrible stutter.

745040206.text: They say that it's a long-term effect of him having fallen from the audience seats and hitting his head at a comedy show.

745040207.text: I really liked that comedy too. I recall that it was called "Judgment," but nowadays, I feel like I can't really enjoy it.

745040208.text: I mean, the kid who wanted to become a comic actor was judged during a comedy called "Judgment"... and his sentence was to never become one.

745040209.text: Poor Armand. What sin did he commit, and who was his judge?

745040301.text: Have you seen the evaluation board? Seems like someone likes those clockwork penguins.

745040302.text: I saw it. It's the one that talks about wanting to get to know Freminet, right? Sounds like someone who would like to strike up some further collaboration, if you ask me.

745040305.text: Oh, we're talking about those clockwork penguins on that table. A diver named Freminet made them, and he then placed them in our store as a consignment.

745040306.text: He's a good lad with a pretty face. Soft-spoken fellow, but he's very good at making toys.

745040307.text: He seems a little melancholy, though. Like someone who lacks something that should've belonged to him...

745040308.text: I know that look, y'know — it's the same one that Arbon makes when he looks at his empty wallet. Don't suppose Freminet's in need of Mora, do you?

745040309.text: Don't be ridiculous. He didn't even discuss the profit-split when he came to talk about the consignment. He wasn't in it for the Mora.

745040310.text: True. But what else would trouble a lad of his age?

745040311.text: Yeah, and he's a winsome fellow, too. I haven't seen the boss ever approve of a consignment.

745040312.text: He not only offered to set up an outdoor stall for the penguins, but even proposed a fifty-fifty split on the earnings.

745040313.text: Unfortunately, one could only call the sales middling. Many people came to look, sure, but there weren't many buyers.

745040314.text: That toy is very intricately designed, but I'd say that also makes it harder to play with... and harder to fix.

745040315.text: Really, I didn't expect that anyone would leave a message about it on the board. Maybe there's a big client behind it, eh?

745040316.text: Either way, we should tell the boss about it. Won't do to miss out on a good deal, you know?

745040401.text: I'll inform you if my efforts at the Northland Bank bear any fruit.

745040402.text: Arbon and Alberre don't seem to be in today.

745040403.text: They took leave, said they had a new idea for toys. Weird, if you ask me.

745040404.text: They usually can't think of anything but their favorite comedies — forget having any thoughts about toys.

745040405.text: What this change of heart is about, I couldn't guess...

745050201.text: It's very s—s—simple and f—fun... D—Do you want to try?

745050205.text: O—Okay! Y—You can come back any time... I'll b—be here.
